recommendation: Keep the source fix. It aligns active element comments and the active example with current References guidance without adding redundant Narrative prose or editing negative invariant-test fixtures.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-I clarification reporting that contained-resource guidance allowed narrative while the Narrative page still said contained resources SHALL NOT have their own narrative; the resolution said to remove the stale prohibition after GF#13870 dropped the invariant.
initial_application: GF#13870 commit a18a11e219deb516933a73c8edf8f8a460f45051 changed References to allow contained-resource narrative and describe rendering behavior. GF#18483 commit 1e886ea379d2668be97b3aaf9b9c03a37c18a974 removed the exact Narrative page sentence, but the later source conversion preserved stale DomainResource.text wording.
additional_context: DomainResource is an active infrastructure resource and Narrative/References are active type pages in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-18483 is the same dropped-invariant change family, while FHIR-5344 is older DSTU1 history superseded by the 2018 decisions. A 2022 HAPI Zulip thread also treated the no-contained-narrative rule as gone from R4.
reconciliation: Changed source/domainresource/structuredefinition-DomainResource.xml and source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-example.xml to remove the obsolete contained-resource narrative prohibition while preserving the guidance that non-contained resources should have narrative.
source_changes: source/domainresource/structuredefinition-DomainResource.xml: removed the sentence saying contained resources do not have a narrative from DomainResource.text comment.
source/structuredefinition/structuredefinition-example.xml: removed the same obsolete prohibition from the DiagnosticReport.text example comment.

related_jiras.note: Separately requested removal of the exact Narrative page text for the dropped invariant and was audited opportunistically.
Older DSTU1 correction made the no-contained-narrative rule SHALL before GF#13870 and the 2018 issues reversed that rule.
